review_candidates.title: Field and Integrated Marketing Manager
review_candidates.description: Please note that the position is 100% remote and we are open for candidates from around the world. About Severalnines Severalnines helps organizations run business-critical databases on infrastructure they control. ClusterControl automates operations across heterogeneous database estates, while CCX enables enterprises and service providers to deliver private, sovereign and white-label database services. Who are we looking for? We are looking for a hands-on Field and Integrated Marketing Manager to build and run a connected program of conferences, local meetups, owned events, technical webinars and expert conversations. Your job is to bring Severalnines closer to the practitioners, buyers and partners who need our products - and turn that access into lasting relationships, product adoption and qualified commercial conversations. Field and community are a core part of our go-to-market direction, not a short-term experiment. You will turn that direction into a repeatable program: choosing the right opportunities, bringing the right audiences together, delivering credible experiences and making sure useful engagement continues after each event. The program supports ClusterControl and CCX, our company flagship products, with the conversation adapted to each audience and account. Your role & responsibilities Build and run one connected program Translate company, product and market priorities into a rolling 12-month calendar. Give every activity a clear audience, purpose, account or community focus, budget, delivery plan and next step. Balance major sponsorships with smaller ecosystem appearances, local collaborations and owned formats. Build lasting community and ecosystem relationships Develop a network of organizers, local hosts, technical experts, customers and partners. Create reasons for people to return, contribute, share their experience and introduce others. Assess existing community channels and focus on useful participation rather than launching new channels simply to grow membership. Deliver events end to end Own sponsorships, venues, vendors, budgets, timelines, travel and on-site or virtual production. Recruit and prepare speakers, shape practical agendas with technical experts, coordinate assets and rehearsals, and run post-event reviews. Build reusable playbooks so delivery becomes more consistent as the program grows. Bring the right people into the room Work with Sales and Marketing Operations to identify target accounts, partners and relevant roles, then coordinate invitations, promotion and meeting booking. Tailor the experience for practitioners, decision-makers, customers and providers rather than treating every registration as the same type of lead. Connect engagement to the right next step Work with Marketing Operations on registration, segmentation, nurture and CRM capture. Route participants toward technical education, product evaluation, architecture reviews, partner discovery, community participation or Sales as appropriate. Agree qualification and follow-up expectations with Sales, provide useful context and track acceptance, next actions and outcomes. Extend the value beyond the event Coordinate recordings, interviews, clips, technical takeaways and follow-up resources with Creative & Brand and our subject-matter experts. Use these assets to continue community conversations and support account follow-up. Bring recurring audience questions and feedback back to Marketing, Product and Sales. Manage performance and investment Track delivery, audience relevance, repeat participation, qualified conversations, product actions, opportunity contribution and follow-up coverage. Maintain accurate spend forecasts, distinguish sourced from influenced opportunities, and recommend where to invest more, change the approach or stop an activity. The program you will run Our Initial Working Plan Includes Two anchor sponsored conferences and at least four lighter secondary or ecosystem appearances Six local meetups One owned half-day event Six technical webinars and release-led sessions as needed Six podcasts or expert conversations These are planning assumptions, not a requirement to maximize event volume. You will refine the mix around audience relevance, market opportunity, production capacity and budget. Named-account follow-up and community engagement continue throughout the year. Local hosts, partners and internal contributors will help extend the program across selected markets. You are not expected to launch everywhere or deliver every activity alone. How you will work You will report to the Marketing Director and work closely with Creative & Brand, Marketing Operations, Sales, Product, Engineering and Support. You will manage approved field and community allocations and recommend changes, while the Marketing Director retains overall budget and strategic-priority decisions. You own program delivery, relationships, audience experience and effective handoffs. Sales owns accepted opportunities and closing. Technical experts own technical accuracy and product commitments. This is a program ownership role with hands-on execution. It is not an SDR position, and you are not expected to personally create every technical presentation, design asset or recording. What we’re looking for Experience owning field, event, community or developer marketing programs in B2B software, cloud infrastructure, databases or a similarly technical business, with examples of meaningful audience and commercial outcomes. Hands-on experience delivering in-person and virtual events, including speaker preparation, vendor coordination, budgets, promotion, production and follow-up. You can manage several overlapping workstreams without losing the details. Strong relationship-building skills with communities, customers, partners and internal teams. You know how to create repeat participation and work with local organizers or contributors across markets. Technical curiosity and audience empathy. You can work with engineers, database specialists and platform teams to develop useful, credible sessions. You do not need to be a database expert, but you should be comfortable learning the subject and asking precise questions. Practical experience with CRM and marketing automation, webinar or event platforms, and reporting. You can connect participation to follow-up and account progression, understand the limits of attribution, and use evidence to make budget decisions. Clear written and spoken English, independent project ownership and the ability to coordinate across teams and time zones. Willingness to travel internationally as part of the role and occasionally deliver events outside standard local working hours. What success looks like In your first 90 days You Will Turn the agreed direction and existing activity into a prioritized calendar. Establish repeatable event briefs, production workflows and post-event processes. Build a network of speakers, partners, community contacts and local hosts. Put audience capture, segmentation and Sales handoffs into operation with Marketing Operations. Take ownership of scheduled delivery and establish a practical performance baseline. Over time Success means building stronger access to relevant accounts and ecosystems, increasing repeat participation and advocacy, delivering consistently within budget, and creating more meaningful product and commercial next steps from audience engagement. You will review follow-up and opportunity contributions regularly with Sales and provide clear recommendations to the Marketing Director. Attendance and registration counts matter as operating measures, but they are not the goal on their own. The goal is to build a field and community program that creates useful relationships, credible engagement and measurable business impact. What We Offer B2B contract with full-time employee benefits Annual bonus based on company results Reimbursement budget to setup and maintain your virtual office (PC, Notebook, Headset, etc.) 4 weeks paid vacation annually Additional birthday day off Paid public holidays in your country Monthly budget for sports activities You can work from anywhere Flexible working arrangements Offsite team meetings at least once a year (we’ve already visited places including Tokyo, Madrid, Belgrade, and Krakow)

Vous intégrerez une équipe transverse dédiée à la conception, à l'administration et à l'évolution des solutions d'automatisation. Cette équipe accompagne plusieurs équipes métiers en mettant à leur disposition un environnement industrialisé, sécurisé et évolutif. L'environnement technique repose sur une infrastructure Ansible Automation Platform containerisée, des API sécurisées et des chaînes CI/CD permettant d'automatiser, de tester et de déployer les processus de manière fiable. Objectifs de la mission Votre objectif principal sera de concevoir, développer et maintenir des solutions d'automatisation des infrastructures, tout en contribuant à la fiabilité, à la sécurité et à l'industrialisation de la plateforme Ansible. Missions principales Participer à la définition, à la conception et à l'évolution de l'architecture d'automatisation. Contribuer à la mise en place, à l'administration et à l'amélioration continue de l'infrastructure Ansible Automation Platform. Développer, maintenir et documenter des playbooks et des collections Ansible réutilisables. Concevoir et maintenir des custom facts et des inventaires dynamiques. Administrer et optimiser les Execution Environments (EE) au sein d'Ansible Automation Platform. Concevoir, industrialiser et maintenir des pipelines CI/CD avec Jenkins et Bitbucket pour le code Ansible et les Execution Environments. Automatiser et sécuriser les processus à travers les API et les pipelines CI/CD. Gérer les API AAP2 et assurer leur intégration avec des outils tiers. Mettre en œuvre les bonnes pratiques de sécurité : Ansible Vault, RBAC, gestion des secrets et scans automatisés. Développer et maintenir des tests automatisés pour Ansible à l'aide de Molecule. Intégrer les pratiques DevSecOps tout au long du cycle de vie des automatisations. Accompagner les équipes internes dans l'utilisation d'Ansible et promouvoir les bonnes pratiques. Assurer le maintien en conditions opérationnelles des plateformes, traiter les incidents et réaliser les diagnostics de niveau 2/3. Participer aux activités BUILD, RUN et à l'amélioration continue de l'infrastructure. Rédiger la documentation technique, partager les connaissances et assurer le transfert de compétences. Participer à une permanence permettant de couvrir les horaires de fonctionnement de l'équipe, de 8h à 19h. Compétences techniques requises Compétences indispensables : Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) : niveau confirmé, administration et exploitation de la plateforme. Ansible : développement de playbooks et gestion de collections réutilisables. Execution Environments (EE) : création, gestion et optimisation. Jenkins et Bitbucket : conception et gestion de pipelines CI/CD. Molecule : tests automatisés des développements Ansible. Sécurité : Ansible Vault, RBAC AAP, gestion des secrets et sécurisation des workflows. API AAP2 : gestion et intégration avec des solutions tierces. Scripting : Python et Bash. Systèmes : Linux et Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL). Compétences complémentaires appréciées : OpenShift, Kubernetes et Docker. Fonctionnalités avancées AAP2 : Event-Driven Ansible (EDA) et Policy-as-Code. Outils de supervision et de centralisation des logs : Prometheus, Grafana, ELK et Splunk Profil candidat: Profil recherché Expérience confirmée en ingénierie infrastructure et automatisation. Bonne maîtrise de l'écosystème Ansible et d'Ansible Automation Platform. Capacité à intervenir sur des activités de conception, d'industrialisation et de maintien en conditions opérationnelles. Expérience dans des environnements Linux / Red Hat. Capacité à travailler en équipe et en méthodologie Agile/Scrum. Autonomie, rigueur, esprit d'analyse et force de proposition. Bon relationnel et aptitude à vulgariser les sujets techniques auprès des utilisateurs. Capacité à produire une documentation claire et structurée. Anglais professionnel apprécié. Livrable attendu

Lead and develop the in-country NOC Leads across APAC (Indonesia, Malaysia and future markets), setting standards and holding the teams to them. Lead incident management and escalation, including timely, clear communication with internal and external customers, vendors and suppliers, and post-incident reporting. Coordinate planned and corrective maintenance (MOP) activities with vendors and site teams, including customer notifications. Oversee backup support for Security (GSOC alarm monitoring, site access requests) and Property Management (after-hours support, vendor dispatch).
